output.brief: The week of 26 Oct (0.41%) is inside the service's normal range. The upper edge of the band is 0.482%, and three ordinary weeks this year were higher (0.44, 0.47, 0.51 and others) with no fault found. The dashboard count matches raw logs, so the rise isn't a counting artefact. The "new pods error twice as often" finding is a warm-up effect. New pods start with an empty cache and time out against the database. This happened at the same size in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy, and it adds only 10–20 errors. It says nothing about a v4.18 fault. Bookings and support complaints showed no customer impact. I'd not roll back, and I'd not mute alerting. Muting would remove the protection for no benefit. Record the week as normal and run the standard check on the following week. Reopen it if the next week is also above the band. I did not rule out the replica move or partner-sync month-end traffic as small contributors. I'm fairly but not fully sure, and I haven't tested v4.18 against v4.17 with pods of the same age.
